thread:
maria: Quick weekly GPU forecast — posting condensed numbers and asks for headroom decisions. TL;DR: US/EU roughly steady, APAC shows a ~240 GPU-hrs/day shortfall next 2 weeks. Need proposed shifts or cost tradeoffs.

alex: Can you drop a per-cluster breakout so we can see where the shortfall is?

sam: Sure, short table below — pulled from the overnight aggregator. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
```
Region      Cluster        Curr GPU hrs/day  Projected demand  Buffer (hrs/day)
us-west     cluster-a      480               430               50
us-east     cluster-b      720               680               40
eu-west     cluster-c      360               370               -10
apac-north  cluster-d      200               410               -210
apac-south  cluster-e      150               180               -30
Total APAC shortfall ~240 GPU-hrs/day
```

sam: If we pull 100 GPU-hrs/day from the burst pool (non-SLA), remaining gap ~140.

jing: Heads up — apac-north has a scheduled network throttle/window on Thu 02:00-05:00 UTC for peering upgrade, could break large live migrations. We should plan migration windows outside that. Also APAC spot eviction rates spiked 15% last week.

alex: Cost note — shifting to preemptible for non-SLA workloads saves ~30% unit cost but increases flakiness. For APAC I’d suggest 60% preemptible for background jobs, keep 40% reserved for latency-sensitive routes.

maria: Action items: 
1) @sam — move 100 GPU-hrs/day from burst to apac-north (non-SLA), start with a 20-GPU canary.
2) @ops-bot — schedule migration window Fri 00:00-03:00 UTC (avoid Thu peering slot).
3) I will draft a short request for a small reserved commit if shortfall persists after canary.

ops-bot: migrate-scheduler-bot: created schedule MIG-4321 for Fri 00:00-03:00 UTC, notified infra-oncall. :white_check_mark:

sam: On it. I'll spin up the 20-GPU canary, monitor p95 latency + KV cache hit for the model tails. If stable for 2 cycles, I'll shift remaining 80 GPU-hrs/day.

alex: Also check whether prefix/KV cache hit rates are low in APAC — improving cache could reduce demand ~5-8% which might cut the gap.

jing: I can run a quick cache evaluation for apac models tonight and post numbers. If hit < 60% we should prioritize cache warming before shifting more GPUs.

maria: Good call. Let's prioritize: canary shift + cache eval. If both look OK, proceed with remainder. Ping here if anything blocks. :thumbsup:

sam: Will post canary metrics in this thread within 90m.

alex: One more ops consideration — before moving burst capacity, confirm burst pool spare nodes in apac zone are healthy (disk pressure / kernel OOMs last month). If not healthy, we provision from us-west and accept cross-region egress cost; Joel, flag if that’s a hard no for exports.

maria: Noted. If cross-region required we’ll include cost estimate in the ticket. Thanks everyone.
